solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Italians disguised origins (7)

indicators.note: a disguise rearranges the letters' appearance

annotation.surface: Italians hiding where they really come from.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'disguised' as an adjective on Italians; it is the instruction applied to 'origins'.
annotation.definitionFit: SIGNORI is the Italian plural of signor, gentlemen, so Italian men.

entries.clue: Disorder led by leader of school trip (7)

indicators.note: the S goes in front of TUMBLE
the first letter of 'school'

blocks.note: to tumble is to throw into disorder

annotation.surface: A school trip descends into chaos, with the head in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School trip' looks like one phrase; the definition is 'trip' alone, a verb, and 'school' only lends its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: catching your foot and lurching is both a trip and a stumble, the sense the school outing hides.

entries.clue: Exonerating unruly peer group (10,1)

indicators.note: the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: An unruly group of friends is let off the hook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unruly peer group' reads as one description, but 'unruly' works on the word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Generation X is the cohort born roughly 1965–1980, a group of peers by age.

entries.clue: I reportedly consider being single (3-3)

indicators.note: what is said sounds like WEIGH but is spelt WAY

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to weigh something up is to consider it

annotation.surface: Someone thinking over whether to stay unmarried.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Single' suggests unmarried; here it is a ticket, and a British single ticket is a one-way ticket.
annotation.definitionFit: A single ticket covers the journey one way only.

entries.clue: Naughty child on edge with limitless adult approval (10)

indicators.note: without its limits, the first and last letters

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child

annotation.surface: A naughty child pushing things to the edge still wins a grown-up's blessing.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' means placed above, so the child comes first. 'Approval' ends the clue plainly; the surface's adult approval is a red herring.
annotation.definitionFit: An imprimatur is an official licence to print, and so any stamp of approval.

entries.clue: Cross feline with clipped claw (7)

indicators.note: a clipped TALON loses its last letter

annotation.surface: An angry cat whose claws have been trimmed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry; it is a noun, a hybrid animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A cattalo is a cross between domestic cattle and the American buffalo.

entries.clue: Bad egg with English kipper? (4)

blocks.note: a cur is a contemptible person

annotation.surface: A rotten egg served alongside a kipper for an English breakfast.
annotation.walkthrough: Kipper is a verb here: to kipper a herring is to cure it by salting and smoking. A kipper is a smoked herring eaten at British breakfasts; the question mark flags the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: kippering, splitting a herring then salting and smoking it, is one particular method of preserving fish.

entries.clue: Youngster dropping an E on teeming Spanish island (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, one E of TEEN drops lower in the word

blocks.note: TEEN with its second E moved down to the end

annotation.surface: A teenager failing a grade while on a crowded holiday island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping an E' looks like deleting one, but the E only falls: in this down answer it moves from the middle of TEEN to the bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: Tenerife is the largest of Spain's Canary Islands.

entries.clue: Boxer appearing in tabloid periodically (3)

indicators.note: the letters come from inside 'tabloid'
something that happens periodically recurs at regular intervals, so the letters are taken at regular intervals: every second one

annotation.surface: A boxer featuring now and then in the tabloid press.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is just true: Ali was never out of the papers.
annotation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was a heavyweight boxing champion.

entries.clue: Oxford University fails to escape disasters and scandal (7)

indicators.note: DIES gets out of TRAGEDIES

annotation.surface: Oxford University can't avoid a run of disasters and a scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fails' is not the verb it seems: it is DIES, as an engine dies, and it escapes from 'disasters' = TRAGEDIES.
annotation.definitionFit: An outrage is a scandalous act or the anger it causes.

entries.clue: Half of planet remains in this (3)

indicators.note: keep one half of the word

annotation.surface: Half a planet left lying about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remains' is a noun, ashes, not a verb; the definition is a descriptive phrase for the container.
annotation.definitionFit: An urn is where cremated remains are kept.

entries.clue: One with artificial tongue is at present struggling (11)

indicators.note: the letters are thrashing about

annotation.surface: Someone with a prosthetic tongue having a hard time of it.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'artificial tongue' is a language, not a body part: Esperanto was invented in 1887.
annotation.definitionFit: An Esperantist speaks or promotes Esperanto, a constructed language.

entries.clue: Brutal pair of boozers in charge (8)

blocks.note: two bars; a boozer is British slang for a pub

annotation.surface: A violent couple of drinkers running the show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boozers' suggests drinkers, but in British slang a boozer is also the pub itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Barbaric means savagely cruel, brutal.

entries.clue: Fled, circled by spooks and skulls (6)

indicators.note: what is circled by something has that thing drawn right round it, so RAN sits inside CIA

blocks.note: spooks are spies; the CIA is the US spy agency

annotation.surface: Someone running away from ghosts and skulls in a horror film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spooks' suggests ghosts beside the skulls; here they are spies.
annotation.definitionFit: Crania is the plural of cranium, a skull.

entries.clue: Spooner’s prophet dubbed “purblind” (4-7)

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a seer is a prophet; its S swaps with the N sound of the next word
to dub is to knight with a sword tap; its N sound swaps with the S

annotation.surface: A prophet given a nickname meaning half-blind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dubbed' reads as nicknamed, but it is the sword-on-the-shoulder sense: knighted.
annotation.definitionFit: Purblind means having poor sight.

entries.clue: Stay silent about speaker and writer (10)

indicators.note: about in its sense of around, so MUM is placed around ORATOR and I

blocks.note: to keep mum is to stay silent
an orator is a public speaker
the setter, writing, calls himself I

annotation.surface: Advice to say nothing about a public speaker and an author.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stay silent' reads as one instruction; 'Stay' is the noun definition, as in a stay of execution.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal synonym: a stay of execution halts proceedings for a while, and a moratorium is likewise an agreed pause on some activity.

entries.clue: Cycling, saddle causes worry (4)

indicators.note: the first letter goes round to the back

blocks.note: a saddle is a bicycle seat; S moves to the end

annotation.surface: An uncomfortable bike saddle giving a cyclist grief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' fits the saddle so well it reads as scenery, but it is the instruction to rotate SEAT.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that eats you is worrying you, as in 'what's eating you?'

entries.clue: Concealment of a mountain sheep, bouncing about in enclosure (10)

indicators.note: ON (about) is thrown out of MOUFLON
the pieces go inside CAGE

annotation.surface: A mountain sheep leaping about its pen, trying to hide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bouncing about' pictures a lively sheep; it means ON, as in 'on the subject', is bounced out. A mouflon is a wild mountain sheep.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: disguising something to match its surroundings is a form of hiding it, as soldiers and animals do.

entries.clue: Provoked near riot at the front (8)

indicators.note: stirred up, so rearranged

annotation.surface: Trouble stirred up by the front line of a crowd close to rioting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Provoked' looks like the definition at the start; the definition is at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal, largely anatomical synonym: the anterior part of a body is the part nearer the front, the opposite of posterior.

entries.clue: Song that’s “Jaggery”? (5,5)

blocks.note: jaggery is a coarse unrefined sugar from South Asia

annotation.surface: Asking which song carries the odd title 'Jaggery'.
annotation.walkthrough: Brown Sugar is a 1971 Rolling Stones song. Jaggery is an unrefined cane or palm sugar from South Asia, so literally a brown sugar; the question mark flags the double take.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is a title, the Stones track; the other is by example, since jaggery is a kind of dark, unrefined cane or palm sugar.

entries.clue: What’s more or less popular music, full of energy (7)

indicators.note: a thing full of something has it inside, so B-SIDES holds the E

blocks.note: B-sides were the flip sides of singles, not the hit tracks

annotation.surface: A remark about pop music being more or less popular.
annotation.walkthrough: 'More or less' looks like a phrase, but it splits: 'What's more' is the definition and 'less popular music' is the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Besides means in addition, what's more.

entries.clue: Benefits of public transport initially overlooked (4)

indicators.note: the first letter is left out

annotation.surface: The advantages of buses and trains being ignored.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Benefits' reads as welfare payments; here it is the plural noun for advantages.
annotation.definitionFit: Uses are the benefits or purposes something serves.

entries.clue: Some dismiss hysterical pettifogger (7)

indicators.note: part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: Some people wave away a hysterical, quibbling lawyer.
annotation.walkthrough: The run starts on the last letter of 'dismiss', which is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A pettifogger is a petty, underhand lawyer, which is what a shyster is.

entries.clue: Evening star located (6)

annotation.surface: The evening star has been spotted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evening star' is Venus in the surface; split it, and 'Evening' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Sunset is the time of evening when the sun goes down.

entries.clue: It starts to trouble every task group (6)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal

annotation.surface: Something that begins to cause problems for every working party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun; it is a word for sex, as in the 1927 film 'It'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a sextet is one particular size of group, six players or singers, so 'group' is the broader class.

entries.clue: Bloodthirsty guards suspended fast (2,6)

indicators.note: guards stand around what they protect, so GORY surrounds HUNG

annotation.surface: Violent guards holding a prisoner in suspension, very quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quick; it is the verb, to go without food.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom matched to a verb: abstaining from food, for Lent or Ramadan, means choosing not to eat, the religious sense of fast.

entries.clue: Sharp intake of breath when pinched by doctor (4)

indicators.note: GP squeezes AS between its letters

blocks.note: GP = general practitioner, a family doctor

annotation.surface: Someone gasping when a doctor gives them a pinch.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the answer's own scene: a pinch makes you gasp.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the quick breath drawn in at shock or pain, like the one a pinch provokes.

entries.clue: Bigwigs exploited a rising tide (11)

indicators.note: something exploited is worked over and put to new use, so the letters are reworked into a new order

annotation.surface: Big shots taking advantage of a rising tide.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exploited' reads as a verb with 'Bigwigs' as its subject; it is the instruction on 'a rising tide'.
annotation.definitionFit: Dignitaries are people of high rank, bigwigs.

entries.clue: Rock is large, seen from below (3)

indicators.note: in a down answer, read upward

annotation.surface: A description of a huge rock towering above the viewer.
annotation.walkthrough: The Rock is a nickname for Gibraltar, and Gib its short form.
annotation.definitionFit: Gib is short for Gibraltar, known as the Rock.

entries.clue: Tiny slug (3)

blocks.note: used as a noun: a tiny is a small child, a toddler
a slug of whisky is a small measure of spirits

annotation.surface: A very small slug.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words change part of speech: 'Tiny' is a noun, a small child, and 'slug' is a shot of drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, a tiny, and also a small measure of spirits.

entries.clue: Blub, spew endlessly, and sleep it off? (5,2)

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of ERUPT is cut off

blocks.note: to blub is to cry, sob

annotation.surface: The night after too much drink: tears, vomit, then bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks sleeping it off as one way to sober up.
annotation.definitionFit: Sleeping off drink is how many people sober up.

entries.clue: Male, rather old ultimately for a swordsman (7)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the end of 'for' is used

annotation.surface: A man, getting on a bit, who fences.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' seems to work on 'old'; it applies to 'for'. The 'a' belongs with the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A matador kills the bull with a sword.
